subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-disabled compaction turn-maintenance timeout key plus a shared command-queue onTaskTimeout hook as the merge boundary for fixing the deferred-maintenance stall?
rationale: The code path looks coherent and tested, but repository policy treats config/default additions, shared queue API behavior, and session-state fencing as compatibility-sensitive choices that automation should not approve alone.

options.title: Accept the opt-in timeout contract
options.body: Merge after maintainers confirm that the default-disabled config key and queue timeout hook are the desired compatibility boundary for bounded maintenance.

options.title: Narrow the queue API first
options.body: Replace or hide onTaskTimeout behind a maintenance-owned mechanism if maintainers do not want a shared queue callback contract.

options.title: Split remaining policy work
options.body: Let this PR address only the timeout/fence gap and handle burst coalescing or shorter recovery thresholds in separate issue/PR review.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in timeout contract
recommendation.body: Merge after maintainers confirm that the default-disabled config key and queue timeout hook are the desired compatibility boundary for bounded maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the original context-engine maintenance and background turn-maintenance history most directly among the available routing signals.
